channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South African Rand: ZAR gains as sukuk plans outlined – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that South Africa’s National Treasury will tap existing rand-denominated sukuk bonds as part of its current fiscal year funding plans, with issuance size and timing still unknown.

item.title: Aluminium: Gulf supply disruptions seen temporary – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey say LME Aluminium fell towards $3,000/t as markets unwound the geopolitical risk premium from earlier Middle East tensions.

item.title: Gold extends gains as weak US NFP data dents Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends gains on Friday as weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data released on Thursday batters the US Dollar (USD) and cools expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Euro stalls below 1.1475 despite US Dollar weakness
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades higher for the second consecutive day on Friday, with the US Dollar (USD) on its back foot in the aftermath of the disappointing US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report released on Thursday. The EUR/USD pair, however, is struggling to breach resistance at 1.1475 so far.

item.title: US Dollar: Services slowdown and labor signals – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the ISM Services index to retreat in June after May’s gain, pointing to broad-based slowing in US activity and new orders while employment remains in contraction.

item.title: United States Dollar Index set for negative weekly close after weak jobs data
item.description: The US Dollar underperforms its major currency peers as traders reconsider hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate expectations, following the release of the weak United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June on Thursday.

item.title: Silver climbs above $62 on fading Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) advances to $62.35 on Friday at the time of writing, up 2.32% on the day, as investors increase exposure to precious metals following the release of a weaker-than-expected US employment report.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Upside risks after sharp rebound against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights that USD/JPY’s unexpected plunge to 160.62 has shifted the short-term bias lower, even as oversold conditions suggest scope for a rebound within 160.80–161.90 intraday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Labor stability favors BoC pause – Wells Fargo
item.description: Wells Fargo Economics sees Canada’s labor market as soft but stabilizing after a strong May rebound, with employment growth under 1% year over year and gains concentrated in full-time jobs.

item.title: Gold: Rebound tests major resistance band – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts note that Gold has held the $3,930/3,885 support zone linked to the November 2025 low and rebounded sharply.

item.title: Indian Rupee clings to early gains driven by lower oil prices, weak US Dollar
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades slightly higher against the US Dollar (USD) in India's afternoon trading hours on Friday.

item.title: Australian Dollar capitalizes on risk-on mood, improving hawkish RBA bets
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is up against its major currency pairs, trading 0.23% higher to near 0.6940 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The Aussie pair gains as a slight decline in hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) prospects has lifted market sentiment.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Softer jobs data supports yen – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao note that weaker US non-farm payrolls and reduced Fed rate hike expectations weighed on the Dollar, supporting the Japanese Yen. USD/JPY fell sharply as markets priced a smaller cumulative hike by year-end and speculated about possible FX intervention.

item.title: What drove the Japanese Yen recovery from 162.60 to 160.60 in a single session?
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) has staged a sharp recovery against the US Dollar, recovering from its weakest level in 40 years at around 162.50 to the 160.00-161.00 handle.

item.title: US Dollar: Jobs data resets Fed expectations – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny argues that softer US labour data should push markets to reprice Federal Reserve policy, shifting from rate hikes toward a greater risk of cuts. He highlights weaker nonfarm payroll trends, deteriorating sentiment indicators and receding inflation risks.

item.title: Euro: Rallies seen tiring below 1.16 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that EUR/USD price action after the US jobs report underlines the lack of a strong bullish narrative for the Euro, as markets doubt further ECB hikes. Softer inflation and low Oil prices weigh on expectations.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $62.60 per troy ounce, up 2.72% from the $60.94 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Mexican Peso : Disinflation keeps Banxico on hold – Wells Fargo
item.description: Wells Fargo Economics expects Mexico’s June CPI to confirm gradual disinflation, with headline and core inflation easing but services prices still sticky.

item.title: CEE FX: Inflation and policy signals reshape regional moves – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes that CEE FX is being shaped by diverging inflation and policy signals across the region.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Hovers around mid-$68.00s amid oversold RSI; bearish potential intact
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – attracts fresh sellers following an intraday uptick to the $69.25 area on Friday, its modest bounce from the lowest level since late February touched the previous day.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Further correction to 20-day EMA might create buying opportunity
item.description: The USD/CAD pair reflects a subdued performance near 1.4175 during the European trading session on Friday. The Loonie pair edges lower as the US Dollar (USD) faces selling pressure due to easing hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) prospects.

item.title: BoE DMP: Businesses’ year-ahead expected own-price inflation rises to 4.1% in June
item.description: A report from the Bank of England (BoE) decision maker panel (DMP) has shown that businesses’ year-ahead expected own-price inflation was 4.1% in the three months to June, 0.1% point higher than firms reported in the three months to May.

item.title: Gold: Higher range forming as Fed risks ease – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Bart Melek notes that weaker US jobs data and reduced odds of a 2026 Fed rate hike have driven Gold above $4,100/oz.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Consolidation within broader band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang notes that AUD/USD’s abrupt jump to 0.6943 was not sustained, leaving the pair likely to consolidate between 0.6895 and 0.6945 in the near term.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Seems vulnerable near two-week low, below 23.6% Fibo. at 161.00
item.description: The USD/JPY pair turns lower for the second straight day following an intraday uptick to mid-161.00s and drops to a more than two-week low during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Softer jobs data supports yen – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao note that weaker US non-farm payrolls and reduced Fed rate hike expectations weighed on the Dollar, supporting the Japanese Yen. USD/JPY fell sharply as markets priced a smaller cumulative hike by year-end and speculated about possible FX intervention.

item.title: Gold stays on track to snap four-week losing streak amid fading Fed hike bets, weak USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) retains its bullish bias for the third straight day and traders near a one-and-a-half-week high during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: S&P 500: Dovish repricing lifts breadth – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists Jim Reid and colleagues note that a softer US jobs report reduced expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening in 2026, with just 30 bps of hikes priced by December.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Jobs setback limits downside – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that softer US jobs data has weakened the Dollar but does not expect this alone to extend USD losses. He argues the report curbs hopes for two Federal Reserve hikes but is not weak enough for a major dovish repricing.

item.title: British Pound holds firm near 1.3380 amid broad-based US Dollar weakness
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, on track for a 1.3% appreciation this week, its strongest weekly performance in three months.
